comments.author: Aurornis

comments.author: qnleigh
comments.text:
Personally, I'm deeply discomforted by the idea that the few mathematicians who have aligned themselves with these companies are able to race ahead of the rest of the mathematical community like this. It is unrealistic to expect Anthropic to immediately share their monetary wealth with the rest of the world (though this is their stated intention in the long-run via UBI), but math is just math. Does Levent really need to take the crown jewel of open math problems for himself before the models are even publicly available? Did OpenAI really need to launch a swarm of 10,000 agents and scoop Tristan Buckmaster, a university professor who had worked on the Navier-Stokes existence problem for most of his career?
This is a time of deep uncertainty and anxiety for working and aspiring mathematicians. OpenAI and Anthropic gain little by announcing results like this ahead of model release. So if they can't restrain themselves on such economically useless things as pure mathematics, it does not bode well for the rest of us.

> appears to use the full power of modern developments on the Langlands program and arithmetic geometry
What I wonder: how do we create new abstractions and concepts? Like whatever “Langlands program” is? That then feedback into the system, and allow for even more sophisticated mathematics.

One might intuitively think that real numbers have a unique decimal expansion but the fact that 1.000... = 0.999... disproves it. Still, it's not too difficult to show that every real number admits a unique decimal expansion _unless_ it has one that ends with a sequence of zeros or a sequence of nines. In that case it has exactly two decimal expansions. This shows that 1.000... = 0.999... is the only such quirk, all the other cases are basically the same, 232.128000... = 232.127999... for instance.

A lot of people just get confused because numbers like 0.23, 0.8, are intuitive and thus something that looks syntactically similar like 0.9999..... also feels like it should be intuitive.
